problem: Zero-shot VLN-CE methods with MLLMs (Open-Nav, SmartWay) depend on 12-view panoramic observations and a separately trained waypoint predictor. This adds large perception and inference latency, is unsuited to robots with a front camera only, and yields candidates that are not semantically aligned with the instruction.
motivation: Real robots typically have only a forward-facing camera, and rotating 360° to collect 12 views is slow. Waypoint predictors are trained on RGB-D only, so they can produce visually plausible but instruction-irrelevant candidates and prevent smooth continuous actions. Removing both should make zero-shot VLN-CE practical, provided the reduced view is compensated with robust reasoning.
key_idea: Replace panorama plus waypoint predictor with three frontal RGB-D views turned into spatial and semantic text, so GPT-4o directly outputs turn angle and distance, made robust by uncertainty-triggered panoramic re-scan and future-past reasoning.
insight: Frontal-only input is workable because depth is converted to explicit per-direction obstacle text and the MLLM is given history and self-reflection. The ablation shows the reasoning modules carry the gain: without Disambiguation and FPBR SR is 19.75, with Disambiguation 24.25, and with both 27.75. The naive frontal SmartWay baseline gets only SR 7.25, so the design matters more than the removed views.
method: Problem setting: one 12-view panoramic scan at t=0, then only 3 frontal RGB-D views (330°, 0°, 30°) per step; the agent outputs a low-level turn angle and forward distance.

Spatial description generation: center-cropped bottom-half depth is projected to a point cloud; the min ground-plane distance per column is averaged into 5 bins (±60°, ±30°, 0°). Thresholds d_close=0.5 and d_mid=4 give text such as 'very close obstacle', 'obstacle at X m' or 'path is clear in X m'. A 12-direction version is used for the panoramic scans.
Semantic description: the RAM tagger lists objects per RGB view (3 lists frontal, 12 in panorama).

End-to-end navigator: GPT-4o receives images, instruction, spatial and semantic text, and the previous thought, selected image, trajectory summary and instruction progress. It returns JSON with thought, selected image, action option, degree, safe distance, a confuse flag and updated history. A slight right shift is applied if the spatial description is unchanged (anti-stuck).

Disambiguation Module: when the MLLM sets Confuse=true (ambiguous instruction, unclear goal, or conflicting visual cues), the robot does a 360° scan and the MLLM re-plans a direction and distance from the panorama plus history.

Future-Past Bidirectional Reasoning: prompts the MLLM to simulate the expected outcome of alternative actions (future) and to compare current observation with the prediction from the last step (past recall), revising the plan on mismatch. It needs no training.

setting.observation: 3 frontal RGB-D views per step (left/front/right); one 12-view panoramic RGB-D scan at start and at disambiguation
setting.action_space: continuous turn angle (e.g. 30/60°) plus forward safe distance in meters

results: On the R2R-CE 100-episode subset, frontal-view Fast-SmartWay gets SR 27.75, SPL 24.95 and nDTW 51.83. This beats panoramic SmartWay on SPL (22.08) and nDTW (41.77), while its SR is slightly lower (29.00). On the real robot it gets SR 36 and NE 2.78 versus SmartWay's 32 and 3.01, at 12.39 s total per-step time versus 29.25 s (42.4%).
limitations: Evaluated on only 100 simulated episodes and 25 real trajectories, with high variance across runs (SR std about 2 points).

Still depends on the GPT-4o API, and inference time per step (7.26 s) is higher than the baseline's. A 360° scan is still required at the start and whenever confusion is triggered, and absolute SR is far below supervised methods.
